Best star trackers for beginners

A star tracker is the single biggest upgrade in beginner astrophotography: it rotates your camera with the Earth, turning 8-second exposures into 2-minute ones. Only two trackers make our beginner list — both proven, both community-vetted.

#1

Sky-Watcher Star Adventurer 2i around $430

The community standard: portable, proven, and it turns any DSLR or mirrorless camera into a deep-sky rig.

Turn any camera into a deep-sky rig.

  • Watch out:
  • Learning curve on polar alignment
  • Payload limited (~5 kg)
Read the full pick →

#2

iOptron SkyGuider Pro around $479

Heavier 11-lb payload for telephoto lenses, plus an ST-4 autoguiding port for when you're ready to go deeper.

The tracker for serious Milky Way panoramas and telephoto nightscapes.

  • Watch out:
  • Learning curve on polar alignment
  • Needs a sturdy tripod (sold separately)
